name: Follistatin-344
route: Injection in gray-market use; virus-delivered gene therapy in trials
status: Not FDA-approved in any form; only experimental gene therapy has been tested in people; banned in sport by WADA
mechanism: Binds myostatin and related activin signals that restrain muscle growth, so blocking them increases muscle mass in animals

article.summary: Follistatin-344 is a large protein that blocks myostatin, a brake on muscle growth. Engineered mice grow huge muscles, but human data are limited to gene therapy trials; it is unapproved and banned in sport.
article.takeaway: Follistatin is a natural protein that binds and blocks myostatin, a signal that limits muscle size. In mice engineered to overproduce it, muscle mass rose dramatically, reaching about four times normal when myostatin was also removed.[^1] In people, the main data come from small gene-therapy trials in which a virus delivered the FS344 gene into thigh muscles, not from injected protein; a six-patient study in inclusion body myositis reported better walking distance, a claim a published letter challenged.[^2][^3] A related activin-blocking drug was stopped in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy after nosebleeds and dilated blood vessels.[^4] WADA bans follistatin.[^5]
glance: Not approved in any form; only experimental gene therapy has been tested in people[^2]
Injection in gray-market use; gene therapy in trials; no approved dosing
Mouse genetics and small gene-therapy trials in people[^1][^2]
Prohibited at all times as a myostatin-binding protein[^5]

blocks.text: Myostatin is a member of the TGF-beta family that normally limits skeletal muscle growth. Follistatin is a natural binding protein that captures myostatin before it reaches its receptor.[^1] 'FS344' names one form of follistatin; it is a protein of several hundred amino acids, not a small peptide.[^2] Follistatin also binds related signals such as activins, so blocking it affects more than muscle.

rows: Dramatic muscle growth; about four times normal mass when myostatin was also absent[^1]
6 treated adults vs 8 untreated matched controls
Walking distance +56.0 m per year vs -25.8 m; a published letter called the benefit claims unfounded[^2][^3]
Boys in a randomized placebo-controlled trial
Trends toward more lean mass; stopped over nosebleeds and dilated small vessels[^4]

blocks.text: None of these tests injected follistatin protein of the kind sold online.

items: **No safety data for injected follistatin:** the human work used virus-delivered genes in muscle, a different treatment from vials sold online[^2]
**Off-target effects:** blocking activins and related signals with ACE-031 caused nosebleeds and dilated small blood vessels, so broader risks are unclear[^4]

**Identity and quality:** large recombinant proteins are hard to make and verify; in one analysis of confiscated black-market products, an unlabeled preparation turned out to come from an empty expression vector with no target protein[^6]
**Long term:** the effects of suppressing these growth signals in healthy people over months or years have not been studied

blocks.text: No follistatin protein is FDA-approved. WADA lists follistatin as a myostatin-binding protein under agents that prevent activin receptor IIB activation, prohibited at all times.[^5] Anti-doping laboratories have built detection methods for follistatin-derived and other myostatin-inhibiting peptides because such agents are available as research chemicals and on the black market.[^7]

Follistatin shows that muscle size can be dramatically changed in engineered mice, but that does not make injected follistatin safe or effective for people. Human experience is limited to a few gene-therapy studies, one of them disputed. Athletes subject to testing should treat it as banned.

evidence.label: Preclinical; only gene therapy tested in people
evidence.text: The strongest data are genetically engineered mice.[^1] Human studies used gene therapy in small groups, and a related drug was stopped for safety.[^2][^4]

faq.a: Not really. It is a large protein, which is why it is harder to make and verify than short peptides.

faq.q: Does injected follistatin build muscle in people?
faq.a: That has not been shown. The human studies delivered the gene into muscle with a virus, and even those were small.[^2]
Yes. WADA names follistatin as a prohibited myostatin-binding protein.[^5]
